amendment.text: Memphis and Shelby County keep the model table's ratios (only footnote e, on service sinks, is replaced) and keep the half-and-half split and rounding up. They change the rules around it: (1) Section 403.1.1 loses exceptions 2 and 3, so the plumbing code no longer carries the fixture count for shared all-gender rooms or the waiver of the split where single-user rooms are provided. (2) Section 403.2 loses exceptions 5 and 6, so the plumbing code no longer says that separate rooms need not be designated by sex where only single-user rooms are provided, or that separate rooms are not required where a shared room for both sexes has private toilet compartments. The small-occupancy exceptions (15 or fewer occupants, business 25 or fewer, mercantile 100 or fewer) stay. Section 403.1.2 (single-user rooms identified as available to all) is not amended. (3) Urinals: where only three fixtures are required, two must be toilets; waterless, trough and floor-mounted urinals are prohibited. (4) Multi-tenant office buildings need common core men's and women's toilets on each floor, sized from the business row, and toilets inside a tenant's suite are not deducted. (5) Toilets must be on the same story and within 300 feet; restaurants and nightclubs in covered malls need their own toilets inside. The building code's Chapter 29, which repeats the model exceptions, is not amended in the building code exhibit read; the plumbing code says the most restrictive provision governs where sections differ.
amendment.quote: DELETE Section 403.1.1 Fixture Calculation (Exceptions 2 and 3) || DELETE Section 403.2 Separate facilities (Exceptions 5 and 6) || 424.1 ... Urinals must have integral trap and visible trap seals. Waterless urinals shall be prohibited. || 424.2 Substitution for water closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Where only three fixtures are required, two of these must be water closets. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closet in all other occupancies. || 403.7 Multi-Tenant office buildings. Common core toilet facilities (separate for males and females) are required for each floor at a rate to be determined by Table 403.1 Business Occupancies. When tenancies, rental units, etc. are to be provided with separate facilities, such facilities are not deductible from the total common core facilities required. || 403.3.3 ... the required public and employee facilities shall be located on the same story as the space required to be provided with toilet facilities, and the path of travel to such facilities shall not exceed a distance of 300 feet. || 403.3.4.2 Restaurants and nightclubs inside covered malls. Restaurants and nightclubs located inside covered malls shall have separate facilities located inside of the restaurant or nightclub. || 401.2 ... Trough, floor mounted and waterless urinals shall be prohibited. || 102.1 ... Where, in a specific case, different sections of this code specify different materials, methods of construction or other requirements, the most restrictive shall govern.

table.source: Table 403.1 of the 2021 International Plumbing Code, not amended by Memphis and Shelby County except footnote e; ratios as in the Tennessee state pack (read on UpCodes' Tennessee copy).
table.office: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 (each sex)

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 25 / 25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace at most 50% of 1 = 0.5, so 0.
50 each. First 50 at 1 per 25 = 2. Urinals: 50% of 2 = 1.
100 each. First 50 = 2, remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1, total 3. Urinals: 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1 (and Memphis: of three fixtures, two must be toilets).
200 each. First 50 = 2, remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3, total 5. Urinals: 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
100 each. 100 / 75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2. Urinals: 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200 / 75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3. The model code would allow 67% of 3 = 2 urinals; Memphis says that where only three fixtures are required, two must be toilets, so 1.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Toilet counts equal the state pack's. The only difference in the examples is the urinal limit where three toilets are required (restaurant at 400: one urinal, not two). The code does not say how the 50% and 67% limits round; examples round down. In a multi-tenant office building the office figures apply floor by floor.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Memphis job sites. Price your restroom, pick the right material and see the Memphis and Shelby County rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Memphis warehouses, hospitals, restaurants and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Tennessee law uses the federal access standards as its own for public buildings. Memphis and Shelby County's building rules also apply a national accessibility standard, in its 2017 edition, and the plans are approved by the office that reviews the project.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** the building rules Memphis enforces require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Memphis sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Tennessee and federal stall rules match:** Tennessee adopted the federal standards word for word, so a stall, door or grab bar that meets one meets the other. The 2017 standard in Memphis and Shelby County's building rules is a separate document, so ask Construction Enforcement which sizes it checks on your project.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Urinals:** Memphis and Shelby County don't allow waterless, trough or floor-mounted urinals.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom is marked as open to everyone. Memphis and Shelby County removed from their plumbing rules the allowance for a shared all-gender room and the allowance for a building served only by one-person rooms, so those rules call for separate men's and women's rooms except in the small spaces noted under the table. The building rules still carry both allowances, so ask Construction Enforcement before you plan either layout. Since July 2026, state law requires shared restrooms in public colleges and universities, state prisons, juvenile detention facilities and domestic violence shelters to be designated for females, males or families. A 2021 law covers shared restrooms in public schools.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Memphis and Shelby County require a permit to alter or repair a building. Their list of work that needs no permit includes painting, tiling, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work, and movable partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches high. It doesn't name toilet partitions. Ordinary repairs need no application as long as no wall or partition is cut away. Ask Construction Enforcement (901-222-8300) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: Memphis and Shelby County Construction Enforcement
page.stalls_intro: Memphis counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and every toilet needs a stall with a door. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets in an office and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school, each with a privacy screen. Where a men's room needs three fixtures, two of them must be toilets. The table shows toilets only.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. An office for 25 people or fewer, or any space for 15 or fewer, may use one shared room. Memphis and Shelby County add rules of their own. In an office building with several tenants, every floor needs shared men's and women's rooms sized for that floor, and toilets inside a tenant's own suite don't count toward them. Toilets must be on the same floor as the space they serve and no more than 300 feet away. A restaurant or nightclub in a covered mall needs its own toilets inside its space.
page.install_rule: Where a permit is needed, Memphis and Shelby County issue it to a contractor registered with Construction Enforcement. State-licensed contractors register their license there, with a registration fee and a surety bond. Tennessee requires a state contractor license to bid or take commercial projects of $25,000 or more. Confirm what your project needs with Construction Enforcement. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who takes out a permit in Memphis registers a Tennessee license with Construction Enforcement.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Tennessee's wage law for public work covers state highway projects only, so on a school or city building a set wage applies only where federal money brings in the federal wage rules. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in Shelby County is $30.20 an hour plus $14.74 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9.75% in Memphis: 7% state and 2.75% local. The local part applies only to the first $1,600 of the price of each single item, and the state adds 2.75% on the part of an item's price between $1,600 and $3,200.
page.buyers_extra: - **Freight terminals and logistics hubs:** HDPE or stainless steel for restrooms that drivers and shift crews use around the clock.
